about.what: The semantic test cases found on the CS-Research-II-Fall-26 branches, plus generated pairs, renamed by checklist code (<code>-<nnn>, numbered by the case's first code) and listed once, in data/paired_cases.json's format (case_id, input, candidate_courses, ground_truth), all run on the whole Fall 2026 Section Tally. `semantic_check` (after case_id) names the check a case tests; ground_truth.checks holds that one code and ground_truth.credit who wrote it. The model reads only `input`.
about.per_check: 8 cases (4 counterfactual pairs) for every check named by its code, K2 excepted (none); team cases kept first, the rest left out. T5 sets the number: the real tally has only 4 chained-conflict pairs.
sources: ben-test-branch: semantic_test_cases.jsonl (Tyler Henry), test_cases.jsonl (Ben P), cart_test_cases.jsonl and input_format_cases.json (Khalil)

Tyler: semantic_cases_daquan_aneesh.jsonl (Daquan and Aneesh Anand), csr2_reasoning_cases_12.jsonl and d_category_cases_12.jsonl (Tyler Henry); main: tyler_supplemental_tests/tyler_review_cases.json (Tyler Henry's reviewed copies)
Daquan-1: DaquanTestCases/C1_01..C4_03 (Daquan; the same files are on main as TestCasesC/)
ben-o-completeness: paired_cases.json, its late_meeting and O-completeness families (Ben P)
Khalil-context-path: data/paired_cases.json, the generated counterfactual pairs (Khalil)
left_out: superseded drafts: Aneesh-Anand semantic_trap_pairs*.jsonl, semantic_trap_t8_reverse.jsonl and Semantic_trap_pairs_v3 (replaced by new_input_thing_paired_all_tests.jsonl)
Aneesh-Anand practice stuff/ (practice and generated variants)
Tyler generated/dynamic drafts (generated_seed2026, dynamic_demo_6) except the 7 reviewed on main
duplicate copies: main, ollama-dev-backend and ben-late-meeting paired_cases.json (same cases as data/paired_cases.json and ben-o-completeness), khalil and ben-test-branch old_schema/ copies
model-run outputs (ben-p_test/, *_llama31_8b.jsonl, results files): answers, not test cases
K2 (instructor): the compact tally leaves instructors out (adding them, about +16% tokens per call, was declined); its 4 cases are credited under checklist K2 `dropped`
about.created: K7 (impossible request) had no case on any branch: created as counterfactual pairs whose right answer registers nothing (an empty sections list): impossible_days and impossible_full. Daquan's C1-C4 prompts had no answer key; their checks were rebuilt with keys.
about.rebuilt: Every team case that came with its own made-up schedule (so could not run on the shared Fall 2026 Section Tally) was replaced by a case of a counterfactual pair rebuilt for the same check on real sections, programs and fabricated transcripts. It keeps its owner's credit, with rebuilt_by and rebuilt_as; it tests the same check, not the original's exact scenario.
about.traps: No input says a case is a trap: SYNTH-TRAP student ids are renamed and prompt sentences pointing at the trap are removed; the build refuses to write the file if an input still mentions one.
about.rebuild: git fetch --all; python finalize_cases.py (after python generate_pairs.py adds pairs)

checklist.name: Hard time cutoff ("no 8 a.m.", "ends by 5 PM")
Partial overlap with a different start time
Chained conflicts (one choice forces the next)
Boundary values (ends exactly at the cutoff)
Shared day, different pattern (MW vs MWF)
Right answer is not the first one listed
Course vs section vs CRN mix-up

dropped.why: the compact Section Tally every case shares leaves out instructors (adding them to every call, about +16% tokens, was declined), so a request by instructor cannot be answered on the tally
